**Finding submitted: missing (confidence 0.72)**

**What I checked**
- **Article XIV (Effect of Termination)** — the entire wind-down apparatus obliges Ono: continuing/transferring Clinical Studies (14.2(a)(i)), distributing during the Wind-down Period (14.2(a)(ii)), assigning Regulatory Filings and delivering all Data and Ono Know-How (14.2(a)(iii)), handing over customer lists (14.2(a)(iv)), granting licences (14.2(a)(v)), and returning/destroying Array's Confidential Information and Product Materials (14.2(a)(vi)).
- **Article X (Confidentiality)** — no return-or-destruction provision at all; a document-wide search for "destroy"/"return or destroy" returns only 14.2(a)(vi), i.e. the one-way Ono obligation.
- **Article XIII** — on expiry Ono gets perpetual paid-up licences (helpful to us), but on termination there is no counterpart obligation on Array.

**Why it fails the fallback**
The fallback requires at minimum a data export within 30 days. Array has no obligation to return, export, delete or certify deletion of Ono's Data or Confidential Information — that is the walk-away scenario ("no data return"). The only assistance covenant available to us, the mutual cooperation language in 14.2(a)(iv), is aimed at transitioning the Product back to Array and is not tied to any data return.

**Redline (validated ok:true)**
New Section 14.2(b) inserted after 14.2(a)(ix): six months' transition assistance at Array's then-current rates, return of our Data/Confidential Information within 30 days in machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter — expressly carved back for the Data and Ono Know-How Array is entitled to retain under 14.2(a)(iii) and (v), so the licence bargain the parties struck is untouched. The comment flags 90 days of assistance as an available fallback.
